name: Primary Button 36px - Dual Icon
propertyCopy: Set the button’s size, content, corners and label.
guide: Component Guide Human View Machine View Overview The Dual Icon Button is a compact, filled, high-emphasis action button built for a leading icon, a label, and an optional trailing icon together - used when a primary action benefits from an icon cue alongside its text, at a fixed 36px height distinct from the standard Button's size scale. When to Use A primary action that benefits from a recognizable icon alongside its label - a branded save/continue action tied to a specific integration or provider. Compact toolbars or headers - where a fixed 36px control fits the surrounding density better than the standard Button size scale. Uploading and managing custom icon variations for the same action across contexts - via the page's own icon-upload control. When Not to Use A plain text-only primary action - use the standard Primary Button - the dual-icon layout adds visual weight that a simple action doesn't need. Low-emphasis or supporting actions - use Secondary, Tertiary, or Ghost - Dual Icon is a high-emphasis, filled variant only. Icon-only actions with no label at all - use Float Button or an icon-only Ghost/Tertiary button instead. Best Practices Only add a trailing icon when it conveys real information (e.g. an external-link cue) - don't add one purely for symmetry. Keep uploaded custom icons visually consistent in weight and size with the built-in icon set. Use this fixed 36px size deliberately for the specific contexts it's designed for, rather than mixing it freely with the standard Button size scale. Do and Don't Do ✓ Save changes An icon that reinforces a label already stating the action in words. Don't A single unlabelled glyph for an action with no universal symbol forces the user to guess or hover-and-wait. Pair icon-only buttons with a Tooltip, or keep the label. Accessibility Icons are decorative alongside a visible text label, so they're marked aria-hidden while the label carries the accessible name. Same native <button> semantics and visible focus outline as every other Button type. Custom-uploaded icons should maintain sufficient contrast against the button's fill color.
